answer: A reputation bond works like a mesa in a meadow: an agent must lock a stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. Newcomers start with tiny limits and earn larger ones only through verified, useful work over time, so a gale of fresh fake accounts cannot flood the market. Each fake needs its own bond and its own history, so creating a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds, and slashing makes that spend unrecoverable.
